title: Digital Agency for Abu Dhabi Organisations | 22 Signals
description: AI, cloud, data, websites, SEO, ads and video for Abu Dhabi organisations, run from London with one accountable lead. See how we work with the capital.
h1: Abu Dhabi digital agency for AI, technology and marketing
intro: 22 Signals is a London business solutions company that builds AI tools, cloud and data systems, websites and apps, then grows them with search, paid media and video. We serve Abu Dhabi organisations from London, on-site when the project needs it, with one accountable lead and working hours that overlap the UAE day.

sections.h: Who we work with in Abu Dhabi
p: The capital buys differently from Dubai. A large share of demand comes from government and semi-government entities, their suppliers, and companies that sell into them. Procurement is formal, Arabic matters, and the people signing off want to see where data lives before they look at a design.

We are set up for established organisations with 5 to 500 staff: contractors and service firms working with energy operators, investment and advisory firms on Al Maryah Island, private clinics and hospital groups, schools and training providers, and tourism and hospitality businesses. Founders in the Hub71 community are welcome too, but most of what we build is for companies that already have customers and need the next stage built properly.

sections.h: What organisations in the capital hire us for
p: We cover the technology a business runs on and the marketing that brings customers in, with one team behind both. That combination of AI, cloud and data with marketing and with video, animation and 3D is what makes us different from a development house or an ad agency on its own.

sections.h: The data rules that apply in the capital
p: Most mainland companies fall under the UAE Personal Data Protection Law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Firms licensed in Abu Dhabi Global Market follow the ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 instead, overseen by the ADGM Office of Data Protection. Healthcare providers have a third layer: the federal health data law (Federal Law No. 2 of 2019) restricts storing and moving health data outside the UAE except where exemptions apply, and the Department of Health Abu Dhabi sets its own cyber security standard, ADHICS.

We work out which regime applies before we design anything, then pick hosting to match. AWS and Microsoft Azure both run cloud regions inside the UAE, which makes in-country storage a practical option rather than a special project.

sections.h: The capital's AI push and what it means for suppliers
p: In January 2025 the Abu Dhabi Government launched its Digital Strategy 2025 to 2027, with the stated aim of becoming the first fully AI-native government by 2027. Add MBZUAI in Masdar City and the wider research and investment ecosystem, and you get buyers who already understand what large models can do.
Entities and the firms serving them expect AI proposals with clear use cases, evaluation, data handling and a named owner, not a demo. That is how our AI consultancy work is set up.

sections.h: Customers here talk on WhatsApp, in two languages
p: Residents and visitors message businesses on WhatsApp far more than they fill in forms. Clinics, schools, property agents and tour operators here get bookings and questions there first. We build WhatsApp Business API flows with AI replies and a person taking over when it matters, synced to the CRM.

Search and content run in Arabic and English. Some people search in Arabic, many in English, and plenty switch between the two in one session. Websites, ads, video subtitles and AI assistants need to work properly in both, including right-to-left layouts.

sections.h: How we work with Abu Dhabi from London
p: We do not have a UAE office and we do not pretend to. Abu Dhabi runs on Gulf Standard Time (GMT+4) with no daylight saving, so it is 4 hours ahead of London in winter and 3 hours ahead in summer. A 9:00 start in London is 13:00 in Abu Dhabi in winter, which gives a solid shared afternoon. Since the UAE moved its weekend to Saturday and Sunday in 2022, our working weeks line up too.

Every engagement has one Signal Lead, the person accountable for delivery, with specialist teams behind them. We follow four steps: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow. Every date agreed goes in writing. When a workshop, a shoot or a stakeholder session is better done in person, we come to Abu Dhabi when the project needs it.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across four regions, in healthcare, law, retail, gaming and technology. The work ranges from AI builds and client portals to monthly SEO, live broadcasts and go-to-market plans.

sections.h: Choosing a digital agency: Abu Dhabi questions worth asking
p: Organisations in the emirate often work with UK and US partners already, and London hours sit comfortably between the Gulf and the Americas. You get one contract, one lead and one team covering technology, marketing and video, instead of coordinating three or four vendors who each own a slice. If you are comparing a digital agency Abu Dhabi entities have used for years with a remote one, ask both the same questions: who is accountable, where is the data, and what is written down.
We also work with Dubai companies, and the two cities get separate pages because the buyers, the regulators and the work are different.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: No. Our head office is in London and we serve Abu Dhabi organisations remotely, with meeting hours that overlap Gulf Standard Time. When a project needs people in the room, for a workshop, a shoot or a launch, we travel to Abu Dhabi for it. We will never list a local address we do not have.

faqs.q: Can you work with ADGM-licensed firms?
faqs.a: Yes. Firms in Abu Dhabi Global Market follow the ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 rather than the federal PDPL, so we check data flows, processor terms and hosting against those rules first. Your compliance team stays the decision maker; we make sure the systems give them what they need to sign off.

faqs.q: Do you deliver work in Arabic?
faqs.a: We build bilingual Arabic and English websites, apps, ads and video, with right-to-left layouts handled properly. Arabic copy is written or reviewed by native speakers before anything goes live, and we plan the structure so both languages rank and read well rather than bolting a translation on at the end.

faqs.q: Which time zone do you work in for Abu Dhabi clients?
faqs.a: We plan meetings in the overlap between London and Abu Dhabi. In winter, 9:00 to 13:00 London is 13:00 to 17:00 in Abu Dhabi; in summer the gap drops to 3 hours. Calls are booked in both time zones so nobody has to convert, and agreed dates are confirmed in writing.

faqs.q: Do you work with government entities?
faqs.a: We are set up to work with companies that supply government and semi-government entities, and we plan for formal procurement, security questionnaires and Arabic requirements from the start. Whether a specific entity can contract with us directly depends on its own supplier rules, so we raise that at the first call rather than after weeks of scoping.

faqs.q: What should we ask before hiring a digital agency in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: Ask who is accountable for delivery, where your data will be stored and under which law, who writes the Arabic, and how dates are confirmed. Any digital agency Abu Dhabi organisations shortlist should answer all four in writing. Ours: one Signal Lead, hosting chosen against PDPL or ADGM rules, native Arabic review, and every agreed date written down.

Book a 15-minute call. It is a fit check, not a pitch: we ask what you are trying to fix, who owns it and what deadline matters. If we are not the right team, we will say so. If we are, you get a written plan with scope, dates and the factors that drive cost.
